resources.string: Your own server: Nextcloud, ownCloud, Synology or any WebDAV

The address of your WebDAV server, for example https://cloud.example.com. Nextcloud and ownCloud are recognised: Dogmatix finds the files address (…/remote.php/dav/files/your-name/) itself. A link pasted from the web interface works too.
The account name on the server.
Use an app password, not your main password: Nextcloud and ownCloud create one under Settings → Security. It stays on this device and is never put in a backup file.
The folder on the server where Dogmatix keeps its files (it is created when missing), for example Dogmatix or Games/Dogmatix.
Only needed for a server with a self-signed certificate
%1$s presents a certificate that Android does not trust. If you recognise this fingerprint, Dogmatix accepts exactly this certificate for this server, and nothing else.
Could not read a certificate from this address
Android already trusts this server\'s certificate
Set · stored on this device only
Not set · needed to encrypt backups
If you lose this passphrase, your cloud backups can never be read again, not even by you. Write it down somewhere safe. It stays on this device only: not on the server and not in backup files.
Backups are encrypted on this device with this passphrase before they are sent. Pick something long that you can remember or write down.
Backups already in the cloud keep the passphrase they were made with; you need the old one to restore them.
The two passphrases are not the same
Every day, on Wi-Fi while charging
Per device; older ones are removed from the server
No cloud backup from this device yet
Show the backups on the server
No backups in the cloud yet. Use Back up now.
This device keeps its server login, passphrase and cloud settings.
Shown in the backup list and to your other devices.
Keeps them in step with your other handhelds through the same server folder
The sync would remove an unusual amount at once. Check your other devices, then apply.
The server did not accept the user name or password. With Nextcloud or ownCloud use an app password (Settings → Security).
This server only offers Digest login, which Dogmatix does not support. Turn on Basic authentication on the server or use an app password.
You are logged in, but this account may not use that folder (read-only share, or someone else\'s folder).
Not found (404). Check the server address and the folder. With Nextcloud and ownCloud the address ends in /remote.php/dav/files/your-name/.
That address does not answer as WebDAV (it looks like an ordinary web page). With Nextcloud or ownCloud use https://your-server/remote.php/dav/files/your-name/.
A folder on the path is missing and could not be created (409).
The file on the server changed while it was being written (412). Try again.
The server refuses files this large (413). Raise its upload limit.
The file is locked by another program on the server (423). Try again in a moment.
The server has no space left for this account (507).
The server reported an error (%1$d). Try again later.
The server sends you to another address (%1$s). Use that address instead.
Cannot reach the server. Check the address and your connection.
The server took too long to answer.
The secure connection failed. The server\'s certificate is not trusted or does not match its address.
That is not a valid web address.
The server\'s answer could not be read, or the file arrived incomplete.
Wrong passphrase, or the backup is damaged. Set the passphrase the backup was made with (Backup passphrase) and try again.
This file is not an encrypted Dogmatix backup.
The sync file on the server was written by a newer Dogmatix. Update the app to sync.
The sync file on the server cannot be read; it was left untouched.
No WebDAV server is set up yet.
Set a backup passphrase first (at least 8 characters).
